explain.say: Imagine the whole world agreeing on one promise list for every person, wherever they live. In 1948 the United Nations did just that: the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, 30 short articles. Look at the board: its promises sorted into four boxes.

faq.q: Why was the Universal Declaration written?
faq.a: After the Second World War and the Holocaust, countries wanted a shared promise that such cruelty would never be accepted again. The UN General Assembly adopted it in Paris on 10 December 1948.

faq.q: Who wrote the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
faq.a: A UN committee chaired by Eleanor Roosevelt of the USA. Key drafters included Rene Cassin of France, Peng Chun Chang of China, Charles Malik of Lebanon, John Humphrey of Canada and Hansa Mehta of India.

faq.q: Is the Universal Declaration a law?
faq.a: Not by itself; it is a declaration, a statement of shared goals. But it inspired binding treaties and many national constitutions, and some parts are now seen as international law.
It means a person accused of a crime is treated as not guilty until a fair court proves they are guilty. It is Article 11 of the declaration.
asks: What is innocent until proven guilty?

faq.a: Human Rights Day is 10 December, the day the declaration was adopted in 1948. It is marked around the world every year.

facts: The UN General Assembly adopted the UDHR on 10 December 1948: 48 countries voted for it, none against, and 8 abstained.
The UDHR has been translated into more than 500 languages.
